# The JVM flags every unidrive launcher passes, one per line ('#' starts a comment).
# Single source: the Gradle deploy launchers, dist/install.sh, scripts/dev/unidrive-jfr.sh and
# scripts/golden/unicode-tree/run-localfs.ps1 read this file, DaemonAutospawn reads it beside the
# deployed jar (the deploys copy it there), and the Windows client mirrors it in EngineHost.JvmFlags
# (a different repository: change both together).
#
# Not listed here because they depend on the machine or the caller: -Xmx (UNIDRIVE_XMX, default 2g),
# -Djdk.net.unixdomain.tmpdir (the host's temp dir), -Duser.language/-Duser.country (--locale), and
# the diagnostics paths (-XX:ErrorFile, -XX:HeapDumpPath, the daemon's -Xlog:gc*:file), which ride
# the launcher templates and DaemonAutospawn under UNIDRIVE_DIAG_DIR.
# Also runtime-gated, added by the launcher templates, DaemonAutospawn and scripts/dev/unidrive-jfr.sh only on
# Java 27 or newer: -XX:FlightRecorderOptions=redact-key=+*vault* (JEP 536, gkrost/unidrive-cli#522). Java 25 and
# 26 reject the redact-key option and refuse to start, while the launchers accept any Java >= 25, so it cannot
# be a plain line here. It adds *vault* to the JFR default redaction patterns, which miss UNIDRIVE_VAULT_PASS.
# A second -XX:FlightRecorderOptions replaces the first entirely: never add another one anywhere.
# Also env-gated, added by the launcher templates and DaemonAutospawn (not a plain flag line): the
# -javaagent of the probe jar deployed beside the fat jar, under UNIDRIVE_COROUTINE_DEBUG=1 (the
# daemon's coroutine-dump facility, archive#613 — see CoroutineDebug).
# Also machine-gated, added by the launcher templates and DaemonAutospawn (gkrost/unidrive-cli#572): the
# per-install startup cache beside the jar — -XX:AOTCache=<jar dir>/unidrive.aot -Xlog:aot=off when that
# file exists (and no -javaagent is armed), else -XX:+AutoCreateSharedArchive
# -XX:SharedArchiveFile=<jar dir>/unidrive.jsa -Xlog:cds=off when the jar's folder is writable. JDK 27
# refuses the two caches in one JVM, so exactly one applies; the conditions are in DaemonAutospawn and
# the launcher templates, never as plain lines here.
# Start with a small heap. Without it JDK <= 25 commit 1/64 of RAM up front (about 500 MB on a 32 GB
# machine), touch 80-140 MB of it during start and give it back only at a later GC: a one-shot sync then
# peaks at ~385 MB RSS instead of ~200 MB, and a daemon can sit at ~470 MB until that GC. Measured on
# Linux with no wall-clock or CPU cost (the JVM runtime spike, archive#624). Java 27's
# G1 already starts at ~72 MB; the flag is harmless there.
-Xms64m
# Pick IPv4 or IPv6 the way the operating system orders them (RFC 6724; IPv6 first on a normal dual-stack
# host), as curl and browsers do. Java's own default tries IPv4 first, and on a dual-stack line whose IPv4
# runs through a carrier NAT (DS-Lite) that path can drop connections while IPv6 is clean: measured on one
# such line, 58 of 300 IPv4 connects to the Internxt gateway failed and 0 of 300 IPv6 ones, and three
# failures in a row aborted a 700 GiB first enumeration each time.
-Djava.net.preferIPv6Addresses=system
-Dstdout.encoding=UTF-8
-Dstderr.encoding=UTF-8
--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED
# A daemon that survives an OutOfMemoryError runs on with dead worker threads; exit so the supervisor restarts it.
# The JVM exits with code 3 then, distinct from the CLI's own 0 (ok), 1 (aborted) and 2 (per-action failures).
-XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError
# The companion -XX:HeapDumpPath (a machine FILE path, one fixed heap-<profile>.hprof per profile) rides
# the launcher templates and DaemonAutospawn; without it the dump lands next to the process CWD. A dump is
# about as large as the heap (about 2 GB at the default -Xmx2g). HotSpot does not overwrite an existing
# dump file, so an OOM restart loop writes the first dump only, and it holds decrypted tokens; pruning
# stays manual.
-XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError
